 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet India have won one Test in New Zealand in 50 years © Getty India have won one Test in New Zealand in 50 years © Getty The first time the senior Indian men toured New Zealand, in 1968 , they returned with something special: their first-ever series win away from home, in more than three decades after entering international cricket. The shores of New Zealand were so welcoming that India returned home with three victories in five games.
 But as years have passed, and Indian cricket itself gained strength, New Zealand hasn’t offered the same warmth. There were times India managed to save Test matches in New Zealand. There were times they failed to close out a game that was in their grasp. But victories in the country have been rare, almost elusive to teams that have gone to make a strong impression in places like England, South Africa and Australia.
 India's last win in New Zealand came nearly 18 years ago; a 10-wicket victory in Hamilton which has been India’s only Test win in the country in the last 50 years. Shubman Gill’s men have the opportunity to change the script; if not for the sake of history, at least for India’s chances to qualify for the World Test Championship final.
 The victories in the ODIs and T20Is notwithstanding, the Test series is where the climax of this long tour stands. The eight result games of the all-format tour so far, for all their preparatory value, have been a glorified build-up, and India would be largely satisfied with how their travelling unit secured wins, even if with ample imperfections .
 However, in the build-up to the Test series, the Indian captain has admitted, “If someone would have asked me a month ago which one of these three [series] that I would have liked to win, it would have definitely been the Test series.”
 Gill had travelled to the country seven years ago as a teenager, when India’s batters came up short against New Zealand’s plans, returning with rather modest totals: 165, 191, 242 and 124. For Gill, that was a showcase of how well New Zealand had come prepared with their plans. This time, however, he believes India will be ready to counter with smarter answers.
 But much has changed for India since then. Back in 2019, it may have been arguably India’s worst performance in a Test series during Virat Kohli’s captaincy era, but it featured a confident red-ball unit. This time, India enter the series as a side struggling to find its identity and dominance in the longest format; more importantly, their fate in the world championship hangs in the balance.
 If they win the two matches of the upcoming series, Gill believes India will confidently hope to make it to the final, even with a home challenge against Australia awaiting. But losing games on this visit could crush those hopes.
 For as pleasant as New Zealand spring is expected to be, the chase to push higher on that table is unlikely to be made any easier by the hosts this November. New Zealand, even though settled at the top of the points table, would be well aware that in the face of stiff competition from multiple teams, they are left with very little room to concede. Even though impacted by injuries and workload management, they would look to ensure India’s inexperienced travellers return with nothing more than the silverware they earned from the limited-overs series.
 When : Thursday, November 19, 2026, 11:00 AM Local (3:30 AM IST)
 Where : New Zealand vs India, 1st Test, Basin Reserve, Wellington
 What to expect : The conditions are expected to be sunny, with mild spring weather, with some breezy winds to assist. Even as teams bowling first have usually won more matches (30 out of 73) at the venue, the average first and second innings scores both have been over the 300-run mark.
 Team News 
 New Zealand: Mitchell Santner has been ruled out of the Test with a fractured hand. Dean Foxcroft, following his impressive performances for New Zealand A, has been roped in as replacement.
 Probable XI: Tom Latham, Devon Conway, Henry Nicholls, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell, Glenn Phillips, Nathan Smith, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Jacob Duffy India: Shubman Gill has admitted that the visitors will be fielding a four-man pace attack while also ensuring ample depth in the batting.
 Probable XI: Yashasvi Jasiwal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill, Rishabh Pant, Dhruv Jurel, Ravindra Jadeja, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Gurnoor Brar/Prasidh Krishna, Mohammed Siraj, Jasprit Bumrah Did you know? 
 This will be New Zealand's 20th International against India across formats in 2026 - the most by them against an opposition, surpassing 19 against England in 2008.
 Devdutt Padikkal has scored 1436 runs in FC cricket in 2026 at 62.43; only David Bedingham (1529) has scored more.
 What they said: 
 "We're lucky we've got a huge amount of fast bowlers that are pretty much all tracking to be fit, which is great. It's hard to pre-plan what games guys might play, but [we're] trying to be a little bit fluid in terms of what happens and workload throughout matches over the next six or seven weeks." - Tom Latham, New Zealand captain, on managing the workload of fast bowlers
 "Very happy that we were able to win the T20 and the ODI series. Nothing like it, if we are able to win the Test series as well. It will be a perfect tour. It's not possible to have a perfect tour especially when you are touring away in a country like New Zealand.” - Shubman Gill, India captain
